body.v: Your parcel from a shop abroad has arrived in Switzerland. A customs processing fee of CHF 3.20 must be paid before delivery.
Once we receive payment, your parcel will be delivered within two working days.

hotspots.explain: parcelpoint-delivery.example is not parcelpoint.example, ParcelPoint's domain. It's the only slip in the whole email.
No deadline, no threat, no typos. A scam can speak quietly.
The link matches the sender, but both are on the imitation domain. That they agree with each other proves nothing.
A small amount, so you pay without thinking. The payment page would collect your card details.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone posing as ParcelPoint. Everything is right except the domain: parcelpoint-delivery.example instead of parcelpoint.example.
choices: ParcelPoint, since everything else is right

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Hardly any. The tone is calm and routine, which is exactly why you trust it.
choices: Very little: the tone is calm and routine

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Pay a small fee through a link. Your card details would go to whoever wrote the message.
choices: Go and collect the parcel yourself
Pay a small fee through a link

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Ignore the link. Open the ParcelPoint app, or type its address yourself, and see whether any fee is really due.
choices: Reply and ask for the customs form

actions.label: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself and look for pending fees
actions.consequence: Nothing to pay shows up. The email was fake.

actions.label: Pay the CHF 3.20, it's next to nothing
actions.consequence: Your card details go to the scammer. Small amounts like this are how they get them so easily.

actions.label: Report it as phishing, then delete it
Reply and ask for the customs form
actions.consequence: The scammer sends you a fake form, and now knows your address is active.

attacker_reveal: No typos, no threats, no rush. Surface clues are for amateurs. A quiet email on a lookalike domain slips through where a loud one gets caught.
